title: Extended Data Table 3 | Red-cell axis and distance from health. The per-row values behind Fig. 6c, 6d, 6e, 6g and 6h, with raw-laboratory and single-laboratory comparators and the later tests of the KNHANES exposures.
legend:
**Extended Data Table 3 | Red-cell axis and distance from health. The per-row values behind Fig. 6c, 6d, 6e, 6g and 6h, with raw-laboratory and single-laboratory comparators and the later tests of the KNHANES exposures.**
a, Correlation of the frozen retina-taught blood score with each of its 19 log blood fields in AI-READI outer fold 0 held-out participants with both routes (at least 380) and, survey-weighted, in NHANES 2009 to 2018, NHANES 2005 to 2008 (Fig. 6a) and NHANES 1999 to 2004, a third era the encoder never saw (at least 8,740 adults aged 40 and older). Rows follow the AI-READI order of Fig. 6c within red-cell fields (haemoglobin, haematocrit, red cells, MCH, MCHC, MCV and RDW) and other fields. The three leading fields keep their order in 1999 to 2004. The prespecified orientation rule was uninformative, so the sign of the score is in effect arbitrary. As oriented, a higher score means more red-cell mass. † NHANES 2005 to 2008 contributed clinical-only rows to encoder training.
b, Cross-sectional KNHANES associations of frozen clinical-only BRAN exposures (13 routine laboratory values and typed age, R7 fold 0) with measures BRAN never used, per discovery SD of the exposure in outcome SD, adjusted for age and sex, with 95% intervals from 1,000 Rao and Wu rescaled PSU bootstrap draws. Rank and Holm p refer to the 16 discovery contrasts. Discovery and replication used different survey years and therefore different people, and counts are floored to 20. The five BRAN rows are all pairs that replicated after Holm adjustment and kept a 95% interval excluding zero in the same direction after adjustment for the 13 raw laboratory values (13-lab adjusted). Eight pairs replicated, and that adjustment removed one and reversed two. In all five, higher exposure went with worse function, which is lower grip strength, lower phase angle or higher logMAR. The raw-lab analog is the same distance or principal axis computed from the 13 raw laboratory values in the replication years. A raw principal axis is signed independently of the BRAN axis, so for shared axis 2 only its distance from zero compares with BRAN. The raw analog excluded zero in four of the five pairs, all but handgrip with shared axis 2, and lay further from zero than BRAN for phase angle and visual acuity with distance from health. No interval was computed for any BRAN minus raw-analog difference. The best single lab row is the laboratory value with the strongest discovery association for that measure, with its own natural sign. Haemoglobin had a larger replication beta than each of the four BRAN exposures for handgrip and for phase angle, but these are point estimates. The note under the upper block gives the computed difference in replication variance explained, best single lab minus each drawn BRAN exposure. Its 95% interval lay above zero for both phase angle rows and included zero for both handgrip rows, so for handgrip the data do not show that haemoglobin did better. MCH did not replicate for visual acuity, and BRAN distance from health explained more replication variance than MCH, with an interval below zero. The note also gives the replication variance explained by the four BRAN exposures together minus that of an outcome-trained linear model of the 13 raw values fitted in the discovery years. That difference included zero for handgrip and visual acuity and was below zero for phase angle, where the raw model explained more. Shared axis 2 is a principal axis of the KNHANES BRAN state and is not the retina-taught axis. KNHANES was used with BRAN before, so none of this is untouched validation. The lower block holds later tests of the same frozen exposures with the KNHANES transforms unchanged. In NHANES these transforms received 11 of the 13 KNHANES fields, with ALT and AST hidden, and glucose was shown for a fraction 0.494 of the 2009 to 2018 route and 0.633 of the 1999 to 2004 route. With ALT and AST shown, a secondary NHANES grip model gave −0.065 [−0.115, −0.014] for distance from health, against −0.058 [−0.107, −0.009] in the base model. KNHANES 2024 rows were decoded only after a fit lock of the frozen 2022 transforms was recorded, and the 2024 grip and phase angle values were extracted only after outcome-free gates. Its laboratory values had been read before by the KNHANES 2024 external test, so only the 2024 grip and phase angle values were new. NHANES 2011 to 2014 (grip strength) and NHANES 2009 to 2018 and 1999 to 2004 (death) are US adults the encoder never saw. Each reading follows its prespecified rule, and the Holm p of the base model was 0.001 and below 0.001 for grip strength with distance and shared axis 2 in KNHANES 2024, 0.490 and below 0.001 for phase angle, 0.044 for grip strength in NHANES 2011 to 2014, below 0.001 for all-cause death in 2009 to 2018 and below 0.001 for both for all-cause and cardiovascular death in 1999 to 2004. In KNHANES 2024 the grip association of distance from health replicated, but the raw-laboratory distance carried the same signal, and beside it the BRAN term was 0.006 [−0.081, 0.092] while the raw term was −0.079 [−0.154, −0.003]. Shared axis 2 replicated for grip strength and phase angle in 2024 and was BRAN-specific only for phase angle, because for grip its 13-lab adjusted interval included zero. Distance from health did not replicate for phase angle in 2024, and beside the raw distance its term reversed sign, 0.143 [0.075, 0.210]. In NHANES 2011 to 2014 the raw distance alone had an interval including zero, and the BRAN term beside it stayed below zero. Shared axis 2 failed its prespecified transport gate in US adults, so it was not tested there. Its weighted correlation with and without ALT and AST in KNHANES 2022 was 0.795, below the threshold of 0.80, which distance from health met at 0.903. For death in 2009 to 2018 the raw distance alone had the larger hazard ratio, and beside BRAN its own term stayed above 1 (1.288 [1.086, 1.526]), so the two distances share much of the signal. In 1999 to 2004 every prespecified distance member replicated and the injury negative control included 1. The all-cause hazard ratio per SD was smaller than in 2009 to 2018, ratio of hazard ratios 0.893 (p 0.001), and beside BRAN the raw distance term included 1 (1.074 [0.967, 1.194]). In the 2024 ceiling rows of the note, the four BRAN exposures together minus an outcome-trained linear model of the 13 raw labs included zero for grip strength, and the raw model explained more phase angle variance. The outcome-trained flexible ceiling is PLACEHOLDER in all three later runs, and Phenotypic Age in 1999 to 2004 is PLACEHOLDER.
c, Red-cell axis beside Phenotypic Age. Every model term behind the Phenotypic Age rows of Fig. 6d. D2R amendment 1, a secondary Phenotypic Age comparator recorded before D2R attempts 2 and 3 and outside the primary estimand and the key secondary Holm family. Its second execute attempt recomputed the frozen direction and reproduced the attempt 3 projections exactly before opening any Phenotypic Age input. The first stopped while reading its sources, with no result. Phenotypic Age follows Levine et al. 2018 and needs C-reactive protein, which NHANES 2011 to 2014 did not measure, so the encoder-unseen cohort keeps 2009 to 2010 and 2015 to 2018 and its axis estimate is not the primary estimate of Fig. 6d. Every row is reported. The acceleration term lay further from 1 than the axis term in every joint model. For all-cause death the axis interval beside the acceleration lay below 1 in both cohorts, and the raw axis lay about as far from 1 on the other side, the BRAN term marginally further, so independence from Phenotypic Age is not specific to BRAN. No difference between the two axes was tested. For cardiovascular death in the CRP cycles the axis alone and both axis terms had intervals including 1, while the full 2009 to 2018 cohort of Fig. 6d excluded 1. Neither cohort had enough injury deaths to fit the negative control. The CRP assay changed between the cycles and glucose was not fasting, so the acceleration may carry measurement noise. Neither primary record prints a worked Phenotypic Age example, so that check remains PLACEHOLDER and a hand computation from the transcribed formula was tested instead. The outcome-trained flexible ceiling remains PLACEHOLDER.
d, Red-cell axis by cause of death. Every cause behind Fig. 6e, with the raw 19-lab axis as a comparator. Discovery expansion part C, prespecified in a protocol recorded on 2 October 2026 before any new association was computed. The run first reproduced the D2R attempt 3 direction, projections and stage A statistics exactly. A higher score, meaning more red-cell mass, went with lower hazards of heart disease, diabetes and all other causes of death in 2009 to 2018 and in 2005 to 2008. Chronic lower respiratory deaths went the other way in 2009 to 2018 only. Beside the 19 raw labs the heart disease interval stayed below 1 in 2009 to 2018 but not in 2005 to 2008, the diabetes interval included 1 in 2009 to 2018 and the diabetes model could not be estimated in 2005 to 2008, and the cancer estimate in 2009 to 2018 rose above 1. Raw labs and covariates explain the score with weighted R squared 0.950, so these adjusted intervals are wide. Descriptive Holm p in 2009 to 2018 lay below 0.05 for heart disease, chronic lower respiratory disease and all other causes, and not for diabetes. The raw 19-lab axis lay further from 1 than the BRAN axis in 11 of the 15 fitted cause rows of 2009 to 2018 and 2005 to 2008, all but chronic lower respiratory disease and stroke in 2009 to 2018 and Alzheimer disease and diabetes in 2005 to 2008, and in all three 1999 to 2004 rows, though no difference was tested. Its interval excluded 1 for cancer in 2009 to 2018, where the BRAN interval did not. Part B of the same expansion found no second eye and blood axis that passed the stability gate, so no other axis was linked to death. The NHANES 1999 to 2004 rows come from the death replication protocol, whose key secondary family replicated heart disease (Holm p 0.004) but not diabetes (Holm p 0.114) or heart disease beside the 19 raw labs (Holm p 0.114). Beside the 19 raw labs the diabetes estimate was 0.251 [0.091, 0.696], outside that family. With the raw 19-lab axis in the same model the point estimate of the BRAN axis term reversed direction for heart disease (1.294 [0.999, 1.675], an interval including 1) and diabetes (1.954 [1.031, 3.705]), and the two axes are nearly collinear (r −0.948), so that model does not separate their effects. The injury negative control included 1. The outcome-trained flexible ceiling remains PLACEHOLDER.

c.title: Red-cell axis beside Phenotypic Age
notes: Hazard ratio per SD [95% CI] from survey-weighted Cox models stratified by cycle with the base adjustment of Fig. 6d. PhenoAge acceleration is the survey-weighted residual of Phenotypic Age on age in each cohort, per SD. Each joint model holds one axis and the acceleration, and the slate row gives the acceleration term of the joint model above it. The raw axis has the opposite sign to the BRAN axis. d.title: Red-cell axis by cause of death
notes: Cause-specific hazard ratio per SD of the red-cell axis [95% CI] for each NCHS leading underlying-cause group, deaths from other causes censored, from survey-weighted Cox models stratified by cycle with the base adjustment of Fig. 6d. Plus 19 raw labs adds the 19 standardised log raw labs and an any-missing indicator. The raw 19-lab axis has the opposite sign to the BRAN axis. Holm p is descriptive, over the eight fitted causes of 2009 to 2018, and in 1999 to 2004 is that of the prespecified key secondary family of eight members. Causes with fewer than 50 deaths, 40 for accidents, were not fitted. Accidents in 2009 to 2018 reproduce the injury negative control of Fig. 6d. † NHANES 2005 to 2008 contributed clinical-only rows to encoder training.

Rank, Holm p, survey years and counts of the upper block of b are matched to report.md here. The lower block of b, the 1999 to 2004 column of a and the 1999 to 2004 rows of d are read through a ledger of this table that pins the three later aggregates and their report.md files. Each printed value is matched to its own report.md cell where the report prints it and to sections 16, 18 and 19 of the results log where the log prints it, and each reading is recomputed from the intervals and Holm p and compared with the reading the aggregate stores.
